There's a lot of parts I disagree with- yes there's a hub with not a ton to do in it, but it's fun to look around when you first get there, then you can just ignore it if you aren't interested in it. And if you replaced it with a menu, I guess you'd have to have all the dialogue with the people there, particularly when picking up missions, over a radio or remove it entirely? And the mission to defend that hub would just suddenly spring this hub location on you with no context? I don't see how adding something you can pretty much ignore can make the game worse.

He complains there are missions that recommend you complete side quests to level up- I will take his word for it, it only said it was a point of no return when I got to the point he's talking about, but then again I did the side missions. I don't even see what the problem is here- the side missions give some loot and guns, but more than that they reward abilities, which may or may not be available for sale from stores later if you skip them. I don't really see how it's fundamentally different from, say, Doom's upgrade system, where you'll be significantly more powerful if you look for hidden stuff- it's optional stuff that makes you stronger.

He complains about "meat shield" enemies, as he shoots a couple of guys that explicitly say <electric vulnerable> and <fire vulnerable> on them with the same non-elemental weapon. He then complains that they do nothing but serve to elongate the fight. Okay, both those problems have the same solution: Don't just have one gun you use for everything, have several weapons- the game lets you equip 8 at a time- with different elemental mods. That is what they add to the fight- they pressure you to switch to different weapons to match their elemental weakness. It will make the combat go faster, and it will make the fights more interesting. Both problems solved.

But while I'm complaining about him complaining about combat being long and boring, does he know melee weapons have charge attacks? I see him use the side attack a couple times in the whole video, but he doesn't charge it and that's probably the weakest of the three. I haven't seen him use the other two charge attacks once.

He then fights a guy with "physical resist" using a 100% physical weapon and complains it takes too long. Fucking hell, man, the game is trying as hard as it can to tell you you're doing it wrong, what do you think those red down arrows next to all your damage numbers mean?

He says switching elemental gems in battle makes it too trivial, while not bothering to use the elemental gems at all in a 100% non-elemental weapon, while complaining the fights against elemental enemies are too long? If it's so trivial, why doesn't he do it and solve his problem? Yes, you could theoretically pause every fight and re-adjust all your elemental gems, but that sounds pretty boring, so maybe don't do that? There are eight weapon slots and only four elements, do you see a possible solution here that doesn't involve inventory management between every fight?

He complains the mods all do too little and there are too many of them- I know where he is in the game, and the crafting system is available by then. Use the goddamn crafting system and fuse some of those gems, thereby solving both problems.

He complains for a long time that you have to "constantly" upgrade gems used in equipment but they're all weak- Again, use the crafting system, and the resulting upgraded gems will be better than anything that drops for a long time. I only do gear checks between missions once every mission or two. He's using blue and grey mods in his weapons after unlocking the crafting system, there's no excuse for that.

He complains he's forced to open chests to get ammunition: I have never run out of ammunition. Try using melee weapons once in a while, the melee weapons are all stronger than the guns, especially if you use the charge attacks, which I think he might not even know exist somehow.

TL;DR: Every problem he dwells on is a result of him ignoring the crafting system, ignoring the melee weapon charge abilities, mostly ignoring melee weapons entirely, ignoring the magic abilities, and ignoring the elemental vulnerability system. Every problem he has is the game trying to point him to a solution that would both solve that problem and be more fun, but he just doesn't hear what it's saying. Basically, L2P.
